scope: Theorem 2.1 (Restricted geometric Langlands) of the manuscript “Rationality of the Canonical Unramified Arthur Filtration” (preprints/Rationality-of-the-Canonical-Unramified-Arthur-Filtration-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 014 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 eaf8e38720714e23), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a Frobenius-invariant union Z of connected components of LocSysrestr b G (X) and an equivalence Lrestr G : C ∼ − → IndCoh b N (Z). It identifies CY with IndCohY (Z) for every closed b G-invariant Y ⊂ c N and intertwines Hecke functors with tensoring by the corresponding evaluation bundles. If f : Z → Z sends a local system to its pullback along geometric Frobenius of X, the functor corresponding to Φ = (FrobBun)∗ is f!. The embedding C ,→ Shv(BunG(X), Qℓ) preserves compact objects.
